units.title: Domain A: Introduction to Dental Hygiene

outcomes.text: Explain basic anatomical terms and structures of the oral cavity.
Describe the structure and microscopic features of teeth and surrounding tissues.
Explain how a tooth and its supporting structures develop and erupt.
Explain pathology and microbiology through study and lab work.
Explain how dental microorganisms are classified and how they cause disease.
Describe how sterilization and disinfection remove or reduce microorganisms.
List what a dental hygienist does in an emergency, with correct protocols.
Define anatomical terms and structures of the oral cavity.
Describe lymphatic drainage of the head and neck.
Identify salivary glands, facial and chewing muscles, the jaw joint, facial skeleton and mandible.
Describe how the respiratory, cardiovascular and digestive systems work.
Apply nerve principles to understand regional anesthesia.
Define dental anatomy and histology, including microscopic features of teeth and nearby tissues.
Mark deciduous and permanent teeth with eruption dates, crown and root formation, variations and jaw positions.
Describe the histology of enamel, dentine, pulp, cementum, periodontal membranes and gingivae.
Define pathology and microbiology through study and lab work.
Illustrate how inflammation works in soft and hard dental tissues.
Describe pathology, bacteriology and parasitology: reaction to injury, harmful agents, signs and symptoms.
Explain acute inflammation, suppuration, immunity, fever, shock, syncope, repair and tissue changes like necrosis.
Explain common oral pathological conditions and disorders.
Classify dental microorganisms and their roles in disease.
List infections in and around the oral cavity and common pathological conditions.
Define sterilization and disinfection.
Illustrate why disinfection and sterilization matter for removing microorganisms.
Describe sterilization and disinfection methods for dental instruments and materials.
Describe principles for preventing cross-infection.
Illustrate how pathogens spread, and use hygiene, PPE and aseptic protocols.
Discuss nutrition: food science, dietary guidelines and nutrients' effect on health.
Describe diet constituents: protein, fat, carbohydrates, minerals and vitamins.
Address nutritional deficiencies and how diet affects dental health.
Communicate clearly and kindly with patients about their concerns and treatment plans.
Care for patients needing special attention, such as oral surgery, orthodontic, cleft palate and disabled patients, and do scaling and polishing.

units.title: Domain I: Oral Medicine and Pharmacology

outcomes.text: Define oral medicine and pharmacology as applied to dentistry.
Record patient medical history, including medications, conditions, allergies, pregnancy, hepatitis, bleeding disorders, and drugs used in dentistry.

units.title: Domain J: Emergencies and Identification of Care Instruments

outcomes.text: List a dental hygienist's emergency responsibilities and protocols.
Manage an unconscious patient safely until medical help arrives.
Care for hand pieces: maintenance, sterilization, safe handling and grasp.
Maintain dental equipment such as the chair, unit, evacuator, compressor, ultrasonic scaler, sterilizer and endodontic kit.

units.title: Domain A: Introduction to Dental Hygiene

outcomes.text: Describe dental caries as tooth decay caused by bacterial acid.
Define health, positive health, dental health and dental education.
Describe what local anesthesia is and how it works.
Describe the types of X-rays and when dentistry uses them.
Describe skull and jaw growth, tooth eruption, malocclusion, its causes and orthodontic treatment limits.
Describe plaque formation, calculus, and extrinsic versus intrinsic stains.
Classify gingival and periodontal conditions, including chronic periodontal disease.
Discuss oral conditions with their features, diagnosis and treatment.

subtopics.title: Tooth wear, restoration and minor surgery

outcomes.text: Explain attrition, abrasion, erosion and developmental abnormalities as forms of tooth wear.
List ways to restore teeth: fillings, inlays, crowns and bridges.
Describe minor oral surgery, including extractions and pre- and post-operative care.
Learn what dental caries is.
Describe the epidemiology of dental caries.
Define health, positive health, dental health and dental education.
Describe types of local anesthesia, including block and infiltration.
Learn injection sites, techniques and contraindications for local and general anesthetics.
Classify gingival and periodontal conditions, including chronic periodontal disease.
Explain the epidemiology of periodontal disease.
List preventive measures for chronic desquamative gingivitis.
Explain these conditions, how common they are, and how to prevent them.
Recall attrition, abrasion, erosion and developmental abnormalities as tooth wear and structural irregularities.
Explain how partial and full dentures are made, cared for and used, and the dental technician's role.
List uses of instruments in oral and maxillofacial surgery.
Explain the uses of apparatus in minor and major oral surgery.
Describe how partial and full dentures are made, cared for and used, and the dental technician's role.
Describe the principles and procedures of root canal therapy.

outcomes.text: Explain periodontal disease epidemiology and ways to prevent chronic gingivitis.

outcomes.text: Describe minor oral surgery: extractions, surgical tooth removal, and pre- and post-operative care.
